scope: Berry-Esseen quantifies the error of the normal approximation asserted by the central limit theorem, giving a uniform $O(1/\sqrt{n})$ bound on the CDF difference.
warrant: The lecture presents Berry-Esseen as a refinement of the central limit theorem that supplies a quantitative bound on the uniform distance between the normalized sum's CDF and the standard normal CDF. It limits the claim of convergence by specifying the rate and the dependence on third absolute moments.

rationale: The relation's predicate, direction, and scope are grounded in the supplied passages. The premise contribution (n-ed32a75acb0c02b3) states the normalized i.i.d. CLT convergence in distribution, and the conclusion contribution (n-08d13cf9a3702bdc) states the Berry–Esseen finite-sample CDF bound. The evidence passages explicitly present Berry–Esseen as a refinement of the CLT: page 8 says the CDF of normalized sums approaches the standard normal CDF uniformly with speed 1/sqrt(n), and page 9 gives the precise bound |P(sum(Xk−μk) ≤ λσ) − Φ(λ)| ≤ 6T/σ^3. Thus the conclusion is properly bounded by the CLT premise: Berry–Esseen quantifies the error of the normal approximation asserted by the CLT, with a uniform O(1/sqrt(n)) bound under the stated moment assumptions. The endpoint claims are also source-grounded: the CLT endpoint correctly restricts to normalized i.i.d. sums and avoids density/local-limit overreach; the Berry–Esseen endpoint correctly states the independent possibly non-identically distributed scope, finite third absolute central moments, positive total variance, the 6T/σ^3 CDF bound, and the Van Beeck 0.7975 i.i.d. refinement. No unsupported historical influence or causation is asserted; attribution is limited to naming and the cited refinement.
